_what: Wire-shape fixture for the public, unauthenticated GET /openapi.json endpoint.
_why: On 2026-07-29 the utoipa 4->5 bump (taken to remove RUSTSEC-2024-0370 at source) moved
this document from OpenAPI 3.0.3 to 3.1.0. That is a wire-visible change to a PUBLIC
endpoint, and it changed the SHAPE, not only the version string: nine nullable fields
moved from 3.0's `nullable: true` to 3.1's `type: [T, "null"]`. A client pinned strictly
Nothing outside the emitting crate could fail on that. The only assertions that existed
were version-PREFIX checks living in the same crate as the emitter, and they were edited
from "3.0" to "3.1" inside the very commit that made the change.
This fixture is the external artifact. Changing the emitted version or the nullable
encoding now requires a deliberate, reviewable edit to THIS file.
_regenerating: If a test fails against this fixture, do NOT edit the file to make it green until you have
answered: is this a wire change our consumers can absorb? Record the answer, then update.
Measure with: GET /openapi.json off a running `wayland-core acp serve`, then scan for
_measured: 2026-07-29, live curl against `wayland-core 0.12.25` acp serve on hetzner-dsm; 18286 bytes, 8 paths, 10 operations.
_amended: 2026-08-29 (FerroxLabs/wayland#305 c2): SessionCreateRequest gained an optional `cwd` — the
project directory a session works in, checked against the operator's approval allowlist. That
is a TENTH nullable site, and it is an ADDITIVE optional field: a 3.1 consumer reading the
document keeps every schema it already had, and a client that never sends `cwd` serializes
byte-identically (`skip_serializing_if`), which `protocol.rs` asserts directly. Three new
paths (/v1/approvals/projects and its {id} form) came with it; none of their schemas carry a
nullable field, so the encoding is untouched. Consumers can absorb this.
Measured against the shape the emitter produces in this tree, not against a running binary —
the emitter IS the document (utoipa derives it), and openapi_shape_matches_committed_fixture
fetches it over a live listener on every run.
